property_summary: After initialization, feeRate in the reference contract can be set to any value up to 5000, but in the mutant only zero is allowed, so calling initialize with feeRate > 0 fails on the mutant while it succeeds on the reference.
After successful initialization, the stored feeRate equals the _feeRate argument.
After initialize succeeds, feeRate() must equal the _feeRate argument – the mutant rejects all non-zero fee rates, so for any _feeRate > 0 the call reverts instead of storing it.
After a successful call to initialize with any _feeRate > 0, reading feeRate() on the reference contract returns the value passed, whereas the mutant reverts.
After a successful initialize() call, feeRate() must return the _feeRate argument; the mutant reverts for any _feeRate > 0, violating this rule.

For any call to initialize with _feeRate > 5000, the reference contract reverts and leaves feeRate unchanged, while the mutant does not revert after persisting the excessive feeRate, so feeRate() can be >5000 after a failed initialize.
After initialize reverts, feeRate must remain 0 (the pre-initialization default); the mutant leaves it set to the rejected value, breaking this invariant.
After a failed initialize() call, feeRate must stay as it was before the call (including the default 0), but the mutant persists the invalid high value.

For any successful `initialize` call, `feeRate` must equal the `_feeRate` argument, but the mutant sets `feeRate` before the validation and still executes the rest when `_feeRate > 5000`, leaving the state variable with a different value than the emitted argument on revert.

After the first successful initialize call, the initialized state variable must always be true and never change; the bug allows a second identical initialize call to complete without reverting, overwriting state.
